title: Tokyo Tarareba Girls
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Rinko, a 33-year-old Tokyo screenwriter whose career has stalled, spends her nights drinking with her two single best friends and vows to marry before the 2020 Olympics (Kodansha blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates). A blunt young model, Key, who drinks at the same bar, criticizes her writing and becomes a love interest (ANN Manga Guide). Akiko Higashimura's josei satire won an Eisner Award for its US edition (AniList note).
life_message: Stop living in 'what ifs' and face your own life honestly, married or not.

content.note: Adult dating; MangaUpdates lists one-night stands, affairs, drunken intercourse (database only, capped; to verify).
Key is 'rude at every turn' (ANN); profanity level not quoted.
Drinking parties are central, called unproductive 'commiseration circles' (ANN); Alcohol, Bar tags (MangaUpdates, AniList).
A 'very raw look' at insecurities; reviewers find it depressing (ANN); Low Self-Esteem, Depression (MangaUpdates).
Heavy drinking and affairs (MangaUpdates) shown as part of the women's rut.

dominant: Satire of marriage pressure on women; friendship; adult regret

frames.aligns: Takes the longing for lasting marriage seriously; friendship among Rinko's trio.
frames.concerns: Affairs, one-night stands and heavy drinking.

frames.aligns: Shows emptiness of passions pursued without direction.
Truthful portrait of idols of marriage and success.
Questions sexist pressure on single women.
Craving for 'what if' shown as suffering.
Satirizes marriage deadlines for women; author's afterword praised (ANN).
frames.concerns: Key's rudeness may read as romanticized.

frames.aligns: Marriage seen as a real good worth seeking.
Shows unhealthy habits as a rut.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Wounded pride but no honor conflicts (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Independent women choosing their paths, under social pressure (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friends, not family, are the support network (blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Workplace with younger assistant and model; age status matters (ANN).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Questions the expectation to marry in one's twenties (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Career and self-fulfilment versus security of marriage (blurb).

folkways.japan: Satirizes the Japanese expectation that women marry in their twenties, which ANN reviewers note as context.

delivery.evidence: Key bluntly lectures Rinko; reviewers call it a 'rude awakening' (ANN); not called preachy.
delivery.note: The message is voiced openly through harsh dialogue and the author's afterword, alongside comedy.

winners_losers: Sympathy lies with Rinko and her friends as they face their habits; Key is a blunt foil whom some reviewers find misogynist.
to_verify: How sexual content (affairs, one-night stands) is depicted; database tags only.
Whether Key's lectures are framed as correct or critiqued in later volumes.
